feedback: Evidence from iteration 0 (60 trials, no finishes): every run ended off track after about one line loss. max_error sat at 0.061 to 0.063 m, just past the 0.06 m limit, while rms_error stayed at 0.021 to 0.030 m and steering oscillation stayed low (0.11 to 0.15). The robot drifts to the edge of the band and loses the tape rather than wandering. The array reached only about ±0.036 m, so the tape left the sensors shortly before the limit. Integration work for this geometry: I kept the baseline gains (kp 4.0, ki 0.2, kd 0.3) and last_direction recovery, and I did not add any gain changes to compensate for the sensor geometry. The controller therefore depends on the sensor span and turn authority you set. Nothing has been measured for the current candidate. Next race, if line_loss_events falls to 0 and max_error drops below 0.05 m, the sensing reach was the binding constraint: keep the span and check completion on oval and s-bend. If line_loss_events stays at 1 with max_error near 0.06 m, turn authority is the constraint: reduce mass. If the robot finishes but progress is low or completion_time is long, the controller can add speed, so the geometry need not change.
requested_changes: If line_loss_events stays at 1 with max_error near 0.06 m in the next race: reduce mass from 0.8 to 0.6 kg to lower yaw inertia (yaw inertia = mass*(L^2+W^2)/12), so the robot can turn back before reaching the 0.06 m limit. Iteration 0 showed the robot reaches the limit with low oscillation, so yaw response, not damping, is the constraint.

If max_error still reaches 0.05 m or more while line losses are gone: widen the outer sensors to x = ±0.054 with 0.027 m steps, keeping sensor_size 0.012 m, so the tape stays in view further out. Iteration 0 showed the array reaching only about ±0.036 m, and the baseline failed at about 0.05 m offset.

If the next race shows turn authority still limiting (line losses present and max_error at the limit after mass 0.6 kg): reduce wheel_track to 0.09 m, which raises yaw rate per unit wheel differential further. The narrowing from 0.12 to 0.10 m in this iteration is the first test of this lever, so the response to it is not yet known.
